statements.text: We know that AI has both offensive and defensive capabilities. With all technology that AI can be used for good and evil. [...] I want to talk a little bit about the role that AI may play in securing our physical borders. [...] how can we use AI to better identify the individuals that are being encountered? [...] how can we within the Department of Homeland Security better use AI to identify the numerous individuals that we are encountering on a daily basis along the Southwest Border so that we are not allowing people into the country that would cause ill will [...]
statements.context: House Homeland Security Committee hearing on AI in homeland security and border enforcement.

statements.text: The bill would also require advanced notification to Congress should the authority be used in advancement of artificial intelligence technology. Given the rapid advancement in AI, it is critical that Congress remain informed and aware of how Federal agencies are utilizing AI to advance their mission.
statements.context: Floor speech in the U.S. House of Representatives urging passage of H.R. 1692, the Producing Advanced Technologies for Homeland Security Act.

statements.text: I have called it the next Manhattan Project for a reason. [...] the cost of being second was just devastating. [...] And I think AI has similar overlay. [...] If we are lagging, if we are behind China in AI, our sovereignty, our national defense is at risk. I think it is not an option for us to get second in AI.
statements.context: House Appropriations subcommittee hearing on Energy and Water Development, where Secretary Wright testifies on Department of Energy priorities for FY2026.

statements.text: It is the sense of Congress that— (1) the heightened terrorism threat landscape and the increasing utilization of generative artificial intelligence by foreign terrorist organizations represent a national security threat, and the challenges posed by such threat are not well understood; and (2) the Department of Homeland Security, in consultation with the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, must take steps to recognize, assess, and address such threat, thereby reducing risks to the people of the United States.
statements.context: Floor of the U.S. House of Representatives, motion to suspend the rules and pass H.R. 1736, the Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act.
